sections.html:
Littleton is the county seat of Arapahoe County, about 9 miles south of downtown Denver. The 2020 census counted 45,652 residents, 20,204 households and 21,476 housing units, with 5.9 percent of the units vacant. The median age is 40.9, and nearly a fifth of residents are 65 or older, so selling to downsize or to settle an estate is a common story.

Much of the older housing dates to the 1950s and 1960s, when the population jumped from 3,378 in 1950 to 26,466 in 1970. Houses from that stretch often need updates, and buyers will ask about them.

sections.h2: Is your address inside Littleton city limits?
sections.html:
Not always. The Littleton name is attached to eleven ZIP codes that cover far more ground than the city itself, so many houses with a Littleton mailing address sit outside the city limits. Unincorporated areas that borrow the name include Columbine, Ken Caryl, Roxborough Park, Heritage Hills and Acres Green, and Highlands Ranch is also allowed in mailing addresses. Columbine High School, which people tend to link to Littleton, is in the Jeffco school district and an unincorporated area.

  • Inside city limits: Littleton rules, permits and rental registration apply.
  • Outside city limits: the county or another town applies instead.
  • Not sure: use the city's Address Wizard and city limits map before you list or request an offer.

We confirm the jurisdiction before anything else, because it controls which office issues permits and which treasurer sends the tax bill.

Small parts of Littleton extend into Jefferson County and Douglas County, so the county that bills your property tax and records your deed depends on where the house sits. Most of the city is in Arapahoe County, so start with the Arapahoe County Treasurer unless your parcel says otherwise.

The Jefferson County portion follows a schedule of two installments, with the second due June 15, or one full payment due April 30. The first installment falls at the end of February. Jefferson County sends a single notice by the end of January, and a payment due on a Friday or a weekend is accepted the next business day without interest. Its treasurer's office is at 100 Jefferson County Parkway in Golden. Call your own county for its current dates.

At closing, the title company prorates the year's bill between you and the buyer. The figure on the settlement statement should match the parcel's county record, so check it.

sections.h2: Rental registration for small apartment buildings
sections.html:
Owners of multifamily property with three or more units inside the city must hold a Rental Registration License, adopted under city ordinance 3-19-2 on December 15, 1998.

Property sizeAnnual fee per property
3 to 25 units$75
26 or more units$125

Licenses run one year and renew by April 1, with a separate application and fee for each parcel. The owner must name an agent who lives in the Denver metro area, can authorize emergency repairs and can let a city inspector in.

A sale triggers two steps. The seller notifies the city of the pending change of ownership, and the new owner registers within 30 days after the transfer. Ask your title company to put the city notice on the closing checklist. The Permit Center answers questions at 303-795-3751.

Most of the Arapahoe County portion is in Littleton Public Schools, which runs Heritage, Littleton and Arapahoe high schools inside the city. Small slivers belong to Sheridan School District 2 and Englewood School District 1. The Jefferson County part falls in Jeffco Public Schools, and the Douglas County part is in Douglas County School District RE-1. If a buyer cares about one school, point them to the district's boundary tools, since the answer depends on the block.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works in Littleton
sections.html:
The process matches a cash sale anywhere in Colorado, minus the lender. We review the property and make an offer. If you accept, a title company handles the deed and the recording with the county that holds the parcel.

We buy houses as they are, with tenants or without, and with repairs still open. That helps owners of older houses that need updates, owners of small rentals who are ready to exit, and heirs managing a property from out of state.

Start with the parcel number or the tax bill, so everyone agrees which county and which jurisdiction apply. Add the mortgage servicer's contact details if a loan remains, any lease and rent roll for a rental, and records of past work on the roof, plumbing or electrical. If an estate owns the house, bring proof of who may sign.

At signing, the title company confirms the final figures, deducts taxes and any loan payoff, records the deed, and pays you the balance. Because no lender is involved, there is no last-minute underwriting condition to wait for.

Owners of houses from the postwar growth years often hesitate over updates that would cost more than they want to spend. The question is whether to fix and list or to sell as it stands. List-and-repair brings a higher possible price but also weeks of work, showings and a financed buyer's inspection. An as-is cash sale gives you a firm offer sooner and spares you the contractors. Weigh those trade-offs against how soon you need to move.

With a large share of owners in their later years, many sales here come from estates. The first job is establishing who can sign the deed, since a buyer and a title company will both ask. Next comes the tax status of the parcel, which depends on the county that bills it. Heirs who live elsewhere should decide early who will answer the title company's questions, deliver keys and approve the closing statement, because a single point of contact keeps the process moving.

sections.h2: What a buyer asks about the address
sections.html:
Expect three questions. Which jurisdiction covers the house, so the buyer knows whether city rules apply? Which school district serves the block? And what condition are the roof and systems in? Answer the first two with documents, not guesses: the Address Wizard result and the district's boundary tool. For the third, share what you know and let the buyer price the rest.

A small apartment building adds a fourth question about the rental license and who is named as the local agent. Have that paperwork ready in a folder before the first walkthrough, so the buyer sees an organized owner and the price discussion stays focused on the house itself.

faqs.q: What county is Littleton, CO in?
faqs.a: Littleton is the county seat of Arapahoe County, and most of the city lies there. Small portions extend into Jefferson County and Douglas County.

faqs.q: Is a Littleton mailing address always inside Littleton city limits?
faqs.a: No. The Littleton name is used on eleven ZIP codes covering a much larger area, including unincorporated communities like Columbine, Ken Caryl and Roxborough Park. Use the city's Address Wizard to check a specific house.

faqs.q: Do I need to register a rental property in Littleton?
faqs.a: If you own a property with three or more residential units inside city limits, yes. The annual fee is $75 for 3 to 25 units and $125 for 26 or more, and the license renews by April 1.

faqs.q: What happens to a Littleton rental registration when I sell?
faqs.a: The seller should notify the city of the upcoming change of ownership, and the new owner must register within 30 days of the transfer.
Most of the Arapahoe County portion is in Littleton Public Schools. Other portions fall in Sheridan, Englewood, Jeffco and Douglas County districts, so confirm by address.
